recommendation: Keep the commit as-is because it preserves the published FHIR-17409 semantics and corrects an implementer-facing JSON example. No further core GraphQL error-handling follow-up was found.
issue_request: FHIR-17409 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core GraphQL issue asking that GraphQL queries support native GraphQL errors instead of overriding GraphQL error handling with OperationOutcome responses.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 14545, represented by git commit bb4b8d2e8a13ee20f5c0bd6c3ce461616eec30a2, which changed source/graphql.html from OperationOutcome-only error handling and a ban on errors[] to native GraphQL errors with optional OperationOutcome detail under extensions.
additional_context: The linked Zulip thread agreed to return a valid GraphQL error response while carrying OperationOutcome detail under extensions.resource. source/graphql.html is in build scope through source/hierarchy.xml and source/documentation.html. Related Jira and Confluence searches found no later decision reversing the FHIR-17409 error-handling rule; FHIR-55105 was only an unrelated same-page spelling correction.
reconciliation: Removed the trailing comma after the OperationOutcome resource object in the GraphQL error JSON example. The surrounding normative rule already says to return native GraphQL errors, so no broader prose change was needed.
source_changes: source/graphql.html: removed the trailing comma in the GraphQL error response example under extensions.resource so the example parses as JSON.
